text:
mohit: Noticed a weird canary regression: reranker v2-int8 shows MRR -4.1% on the Spanish holdout (cohort=es-2025). NDCG ~flat. Problem concentrated in very short Spanish queries (<=4 tokens) and queries with clitics (e.g., \"damelo\", \"cómo\'s\"). Anyone free to eyeball?

sara: Oh no. Can you paste the small slice table?

mohit: quick summary + s3 link: s3://bench/rerank/6001234567/summary.csv
```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1,spanish_short_mrr
float32,es-2025,0.612,0.481,0.50,0.463
int8,es-2025,0.610,0.462,0.43,0.445
float32,global-2025,0.628,0.505,0.52,0.502
int8,global-2025,0.627,0.503,0.51,0.501
```

li: That's a sizable concentrated drop on the Spanish short-slice. Two likely suspects: tokenizer/subword boundary behaviour for clitics and punctuation, or last-layer quant scaling interacting with subword embeddings skew. Did the int8 build change tokenizer normalization maps?

mohit: Canary commit included a micro-PR that merged a unicode normalization table (nfkc) in the quant branch to reduce rare unicode variants. float run used nfkd historically. I missed that.

jules: That could definitely change tokenization for Spanish clitics and accent marks. Also check if we applied a new BPE merge rule in the quant branch. Those subtle token boundary changes can move little mass between tokens on short queries and flip top1.

sara: We need a tokenizer-parity diff across the es-2025 short-query subset. Also do ablations: (A) int8 but force float tokenizer (parity), (B) int8 mixed-last-layer (float final linear), (C) float but apply quant normalization maps to see config impact.

mohit: Kicked off parity + ablations on 8k Spanish short queries. Jobs: 6001234575 (parity), 6001234586 (A), 6001234597 (B), 6001234608 (C). eval-bot: starting bootstrap CI for es-2025 (1000 resamples).

eval-bot: Jobs queued. Bootstrap CI job 6001234610 started.

li: Also please export a per-query disagreement dump (top-5) for the 200 highest-MRR-impact queries. Looking for patterns: accent vs no-accent, clitic merges, punctuation like inverted question marks.

mohit: Uploaded disagree_200.jsonl and pasted one anonymized example below:
```
query: "dámelo ahora"
float_top3: [doc_A (faq), doc_B (howto), doc_C]
int8_top3:   [doc_B, doc_A, doc_C]
notes: float tokens: ["dá","me","lo"]; int8 tokens: ["da","mélo"] -> different embeddings and score order flips
```

jules: Oof that token split is exactly the problem. The nfkc vs nfkd normalizer changed where the accent attaches and the BPE boundary.

sara: Early ablation results?

mohit: Parity run (force float tokenizer) recovers ~2.6% MRR on the spanish_short slice. A (int8 + float tokenizer) recovers ~2.7%, B (mixed-last-layer) recovers ~0.9%, C (float with quant-norm) drops similarly to int8 baseline. Bootstrap CI: float MRR 0.481 (95% CI [0.474,0.488]), int8 0.462 (95% CI [0.455,0.469]). Parity ablation MRR 0.479 (95% CI [0.472,0.486]).

li: Clear signal: tokenizer normalization mismatch is primary. Last-layer quantization contributes smaller residual. Action items: revert normalization map change in quant branch for now; add a per-language tokenizer-parity CI check to the canary harness (fail if tokenization hashes differ for >0.1% tokens in any language slice).

jules: Also propose adding a small Spanish pre-token canonicalizer that normalizes clitics and common contractions to stable forms before tokenization for the medical/legal Spanish cohorts where short queries matter. We should evaluate if canonicalizer harms other cohorts.

sara: Add to rollout checklist: \"language-specific token parity check\" and \"mixed-last-layer smoke ablation for int8\". I'll file a short GT ticket RERANK-ES-117 and add to reranker-onboard docs.

mohit: On it. Reverting quant-branch normalization now and re-running full canary after revert + parity CI. ETA ~45m.

eval-bot: Bootstrap CI complete: es-2025 float MRR 0.481 (95% CI [0.474,0.488]), int8 0.462 (95% CI [0.455,0.469]) — gap outside sampling noise.

deploy-bot: Reminder: dedicated canary gating rules: if any language-slice MRR drops >1.5% and gap outside bootstrap CI, fail rollout and require triage.

li: Good. Once revert is in place, re-run and also run mixed-last-layer ablation as a quick rollback mitigation if needed for certain customers.

jules: One more thought: add a micro-metric \"subword_stability\" = fraction of queries where tokenization differs between builds; show by language and make it visible in the canary dashboard. That would have flagged this earlier.

sara: Agree. I'll sketch the dashboard change and add ticket RERANK-ES-118 for subword_stability metric.

mohit: Thanks all. Will post re-run numbers here. Ping me for early access to the disagree dump. :thumbsup:
